observations: A pink-lavender spiral sits upper-left on the head, with radiating dark, red, and gray lines fanning outward across the full width of the image.
Two large oval eye shapes contain concentric rings of green, purple, and white, flanking a vertical teal stripe running down the center of the face.
A tooth-filled mouth at the bottom shows jagged white triangular teeth between red lips, with scattered angular purple and pink marks filling the surrounding background.
reading: The face stares out through layered rings of color, its spiral crown pulling the eye upward while bared teeth anchor the composition below. The teal stripe splits the image into halves that don't quite mirror each other—one eye wider, one more buried in overlapping lines. The effect reads as alarm or confrontation, a face caught mid-shout against clashing yellows, pinks, and blues.
contextAngle: In the owned Scrimshaw numbered family, this sits between Scrimshaw6 and Scrimshaw8. Scrimshaw6 uses a quieter yellow ground with looser blue outlines; Scrimshaw7 packs the frame more densely and introduces the spiral motif and exposed teeth absent from that neighbor.

connections.reason: Both center a face on a warm ground, but Scrimshaw6 leaves open yellow space around blue outlines while Scrimshaw7 fills nearly every gap with radiating lines and saturated marks.
Both show bared zigzag teeth and asymmetric eye shapes built from overlapping colored outlines, linking the collector's cross-collection interest in shared visual intensity.

lookingQuestion: How does the pink spiral at the top of the head relate to the concentric rings inside the eyes—do they seem to echo each other, or does the spiral suggest a different kind of motion?
ambiguities: Small angular shapes in the background (triangles, rectangles) may be secondary faces or abstract marks; their role is unclear.
Whether the teal vertical stripe reads as a nose or a dividing boundary depends on viewing distance.
